newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadians less dependent on government in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Canadians less dependent on government in 1995.

text.p: Canadian taxpayers relied less on government benefits as a source of income in 1995 than in 1994, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
On average, taxpayers received C$26.60 in government transfer payments for every C$100 of employment income earned in 1995, down from C$26.85 in 1994 and C$26.92 in 1993, the federal agency said.
Although 1995 was the second consecutive year of decline, the economic dependency ratio was still 31 percent higher than the level in 1990, StatsCan said.
The declines in 1995 and 1994 stemmed mainly from changes to unemployment insurance, the agency said.
Women were more dependent on government than men in 1995. Women on average received C$36.05 in transfer payments for every C$100 in employment income, compared with C$21.53 for men, StatsCan said.
About one quarter of payments for women came from old age security benefits, while one-third of transfer payments for men came from private pensions, the agency said.
Overall, government pensions accounted for the largest share of transfer payments at 37 percent, followed by private pensions at 26 percent.
Public and private pension benefits were expected to dominate government transfer payments in the future with the aging of Canada's population, StatsCan said.
